commentary:
Energy is the story this morning. Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz are escalating — with Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia adding to the mix — and the products complex is doing the heavy lifting: gasoil surged 6.1%, heating oil 3.5% and RBOB 2.75%, with Brent up 1.25% through $101 and Henry Hub and TTF both firmer. Diesel is the pressure point — tight refinery capacity is seen keeping distillate prices elevated through 2027, cracks jumped again, and the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 is threatening the US Gulf Coast.

Notably, Brent puts have outpaced calls for 14 straight sessions, so positioning was leaning the wrong way into this flare-up. The transmission is classic war-driven inflation: bonds sold off globally, with the US long bond -0.8%, Ultras -1%, and the curve bear-steepening as 2s barely moved. Fed minutes today are in focus with markets still debating hikes rather than cuts, US mortgage rates just hit 7.49% — a near three-year high — and the IMF is warning AI investment is lifting both growth and inflation just as debt loads swell. Europe looks worse: OATs fell over 1% on fiscal and political risk, the euro slid against all G10 peers as traders rotate bearish bets away from the dollar, and Euro Stoxx futures dropped 1.5% with banks off 2.7%.

Higher real yields and a firm dollar hit precious metals — gold -1.1%, silver -1.9%, platinum -3.6% — overwhelming any haven bid. Equity index futures are modestly lower, with AI-bubble warnings (Dalio) and a reported $40bn SpaceX debt raise for Nvidia chips keeping the capex-sustainability debate alive for the Nasdaq.
